thread:
Maria G: Heads up — we have a customer escalation. After last night's canary (feature flag: `kernel-path-v2`), hosted API error rate climbed ~7% 5xx across us-west-2. Customer reported timeouts + billing spikes.

Jon S: seeing alerts too, spike started ~23:07 UTC. Alert summary: increased 502/504 & gateway timeouts. Link to alert: https://alerts.redwood.local/alert/abc123

Lee: quick check — can we confirm the canary rollout percentage and which routes were targeted? I think the canary touched the multi-tenant inference ingress.

EngOps: canary was 10% traffic in us-west-2, config selector `route: inference-global`. Rolled at 22:50 UTC. No other regions touched.

Maria G: customer repro steps they sent: 1) POST /v1/generate with model=rw-large, 2) include long context (~6k tokens), 3) repeat during peak. They saw 502s and timeouts.

Lee: logs show gateway returning upstream timeout to client: 
```
upstream request timed out (context deadline exceeded)
route=inference-global kernel=kernel-path-v2
correlation_id=txn-9b7f
```

Jon S: interesting — kernel-path-v2 changes kernel selection for long sequences. Could be KVCACHE behavior under sustained load. Any CPU/GPU saturation?

sre-oncall: host metrics look fine on GPU utilization, but redis K/V cache errors spike coincident with 5xxs (redis connection timeouts). Possible cascading failure: new kernel increases mem pressure causing more cache misses hitting redis.

Maria G: customer also reported billing anomalies — retries caused higher token counts. We need to prioritize rollback on the canary and notify the customer.

EngOps: propose rollback of feature flag to previous kernel path for us-west-2 only. Suggested command (LaunchDarkly): 
```
# rollback to v1 for us-west-2
ldctl set kernel-path-v2 target=0 region=us-west-2 --actor=EngOps
```

Jon S: before rollback can we patch a temporary shedder to limit long-context requests to 10 rps per tenant? If we can reduce load, redis might stabilize.

Lee: good idea. Patching proxy with rate limit: 
```
kubectl patch configmap ingress-ratelimit -n infra --patch '{"data":{"long_ctx_rps":"10"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/api-gateway -n infra
```

sre-oncall: applying rate limit now. Patch started. Rolling restart in progress.

support-bot: incident: #INC-2026 opened, sev: high, affected: hosted inference (us-west-2), initial responder: sre-oncall.

Maria G: I'm going to message the customer with the mitigation plan: temporary rate limit + rolling rollback if we don't see immediate improvement.

EngOps: rollback command executed at 23:12 UTC. Canary traffic in us-west-2 reverted to kernel-path-v1.

Jon S: after rollback, 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~4 minutes. Redis timeouts decreased. Customers confirm reduced errors.

Lee: we should add an integration test that exercises long-context + kernel-path-v2 in a staging load test before any future rollout. Also add a guard in the rollout pipeline to require redis latency < 50ms under synthetic load.

Maria G: agreed. Action items: 1) postmortem runbook (owner: Lee), 2) add gating tests (owner: Jon S), 3) customer follow-up and billing credit assessment (owner: Maria G).

sre-oncall: logging the handoff. Moving incident to postmortem queue. :white_check_mark:

Jon S: quick note — correlation id from customer txn: `txn-9b7f` retained for follow-up.

Maria G: thanks team. Closing coordination here, I'll update the customer thread and start the billing review.
